A second easter egg, the accessibility rule the first one carried reversed for the one case it was wrong about, and two rules from a settings-card report.

**Adopting apps:** `DEFAULT_MOTION` is `subtle`, not `wild`. If you shipped the old default, migrate any stored value that used to name the top level before you change it, because moving a default is not moving a choice.

## ✨ Added

- **`disco`, the colour engine's own egg: the eight rainbow colours step one position every second**, so every hued element moves to the next colour together while nothing else changes. It animates nothing: no keyframes, no new classes, no compositing layer. It steps the rotation offset rainbow already carried. `applyDisco()`, `discoTap()` and the three constants are in `reference/appearance.ts`.
- **The gesture: turn Rainbow Mode on five times within three seconds of each other.** Only turn-ons count, which halves the clicks and leaves the gesture ending with rainbow ON, the one state where a walking palette is visible at all. A reward that arrives invisible is a bug report waiting to happen.

## 🎨 Design

- **A behaviour-changing easter egg may outrank a preference that protects people from things they did not choose.** Reverses what the storm's own entry said. The three levels a picker offers keep obeying `prefers-reduced-motion` unconditionally, because nobody who set it went looking for them. Five taps on an option already chosen is not a value anybody inherited.
- **Where that exemption lives is the whole design.** In the `reduce` block, which swaps in gentler substitutes rather than switching motion off, and those substitutes are what make the storm a storm. Not in the `no-preference` block, which holds the press and the spinner.
- **Exempting is half of it; restoring is the half that gets forgotten.** The full rule sits in the block the media query replaced, so an exemption alone leaves the element quieter than the substitute it removed. Where its resting state is invisible, it goes entirely and nothing takes its place.
- **Both eggs stop at anything continuous.** Wanting more movement is not wanting something that never stops.
- **A gesture needs a time window when its component motion is ordinary.** Tapping a chosen option is not something anybody does by accident; toggling a mode on and off is how you compare two looks.
- **The default moved to `subtle`, because the top of the range stopped being polish.** Once distance and curve became per-level tokens, `wild` tilted and scaled the whole route wrapper while the cards inside staggered in on their own transforms. One engine painted that as a tremble plus a green flash out of uninitialised layer memory. Nobody asked for it; it was what shipped.
- **A per-second writer is what tests whether an app's hue coverage is real.** A hue arrives as an inline style computed during render, so an element only recolours when its component renders again. Subscribe once above the routes. A setting only ever changed on one screen hides every missing subscription until something changes it from elsewhere.
- **A settings card CONFIGURES; the shell OPERATES.** Rule 22. A card that sets something up does not also carry the buttons that act on the live session. On a form with unsaved fields, those are the two controls that throw the form away, and one of them duplicated what the shell already offered.
- **Removing an operation from a card must not remove the CAPABILITY.** The test before deleting such a button is "where does this live once it is gone": another surface, or the action that implies it. Signing every other session out moved into changing the password, which is what somebody changing it out of suspicion assumed was happening.
- **The control that starts an enrolment is named for the act, and every such control is named the same.** *Enable* on one card and *Add passkey* on the next made a reader work out whether the different wording meant a different thing. It does not.
- **A control named that way must carry a glyph**, because the glyph is then what tells two same-worded buttons apart. It is picked from the meaning of the capability, not from the shared verb.
- **That word is a per-language LOOKUP of what the app already says elsewhere**, never a fresh translation, or one language ends up with two words for one act.
